Spec 09 Better Graphics, reopened (#35) — semantic diff

Branch feature/better-graphicsBase bccd2ed (the first close and PR #36)Head f10d71c Target mainDate 2026-11-22 Commits 10Files 78 · +3967 / −159 (four delivered pictures, 4.9 MB of PNG) Written by REVIEW: + CODE REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

The second review of spec 09: the reopening for the author's request — two new fighters from his pictures (part C), camera views (part V) and brighter worlds with lighting presets (part L). Range bccd2ed..f10d71c: the requirements revision and re-plan and Steps 21–29 (D20–D31). The first review (2026-11-22_better-graphics.html) covered Steps 1–20.

  • Flarekid (Legendary, plays like Blaze) and Echo (Mythic, plays like Luna) are unlocked for every save and shown as the author's pictures on an outlined, camera-facing quad with a soft shadow; their card pictures are on the cards and skin buttons; they breathe and bob on the pedestal, hop, lean, flip, flash, show a muzzle star and tip over in play, and fade in cover.
  • Every fighter on a pedestal pops in with sparks and a halo in its rarity colour (home, fighter screen, result).
  • V and 1–4 switch Classic, Close, Behind and Overview; L switches Bright day (the default), Golden sunset, Neon night, Candy pop and Classic, K a saturation boost; a toast names each; kept while the game is open.
  • Both worlds are brighter with four new kinds of decoration each (blossoms, flags, birds, a stream; fireflies, pulsing crystals, waterfalls, turning islands), no colliders, the layouts unchanged.
  • 516 of 516 tests pass, lint and check_tools.ps1 are clean, the web export grows by 0.73 MB (the pictures 0.67 MB, C11 ≤ 1.0 MB) to 41,244,423 bytes, the author's untracked art stays out; server/ and ui/ unchanged. Five findings, none Blocking: in Overview a picture fighter's health bar can show under him.

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups — no Blocking finding; findings 1–3 to fix now, 4–5 plan decisions. Accepted as deferred (not findings): the iPad check of the reopened parts (L8, G14), the image tool for LICENSES.md (C9), more pictures or a 3D model (C8), a touch button for views (V6) and the author's newer art (D31).

Author Q&A

Why a picture on a camera-facing quad instead of the delivered Sprite3D scenes?
D21: a Sprite3D cannot draw an outline of a fixed pixel width, flash, flip or fade. cutout.gdshader turns the quad to the camera in the vertex shader (the rig's yaw no longer matters), rings the picture's alpha for the outline and has the uniforms flash, fade, flip, tilt and tip; FighterModel's rig/body keep the idle, run and recoil code working. The delivered scenes stay in characters/ and out of the export.
Why does the camera never turn in the Behind view?
D25/V4 (Q12): with a fixed yaw (always looking north) the movement keys keep their screen direction in every view and the picture fighters still face the camera. Behind stands 6 m behind the fighter at the height where its line to a point 4 m ahead is 28 degrees down (Step 25 Notes).
How do the lighting presets keep each world's own look?
D27: WorldLighting remembers the world's own sun, ambient and sky after the world is built, applies a preset to a fresh copy of the environment (the scene's shared one is never changed) and keeps 30 % of the world's colours (WORLD_SHARE). Classic brings the world's light back exactly; glow is on only in Neon night (checked on the desktop and in the web export).
What keeps the author's newer art out of git and the web export?
D22/D31: .gitignore names the zips and scenes/blaze_godot/; export_presets.cfg's exclude_filter names the delivery's preview files and characters/*_new/*, characters/magmax*/* and characters/*.zip. A clean export at f10d71c and Step 29's working-tree export are both 41,244,423 bytes; the .pck holds no excluded name.

Highlights

1 · The bar over a picture fighter

hack_star_godot/scenes/cutout/cutout_fighters.gd:82-99 · 65b7ff3 · Steps 22, 25 · C6, V5, D21

82## How high over the feet (metres, straight up) a point shows on screen level with the top of
83## the picture, seen by a camera at `camera` from feet at `feet` (world): the picture stands
84## parallel to the screen and shrinks by part of the foreshortening; a point straight up also
85## comes nearer to a camera that looks down, so near the camera it climbs the screen faster.
86static func top_height(fighter_id: String, camera: Transform3D, feet: Vector3) -> float:
87 var up_y: float = clampf(camera.basis.y.y, 0.1, 1.0)
88 var height: float = FIGHTERS[fighter_id]["height"]
89 var picture: float = height * lerpf(1.0, up_y, FORESHORTEN)
90 var seen: Vector3 = camera.affine_inverse() * feet
91 if seen.z > -0.1:
92 return picture / up_y
93 # The top's screen slope (up over depth); a point `h` straight up has the same slope when
94 # `h` = picture / (up_y + slope · forward_y).
95 var slope: float = (seen.y + picture) / -seen.z
96 return picture / maxf(up_y + slope * camera.basis.z.y, 0.1)
97
98
99## Builds the picture quad into `model`'s body (the model is already cleared by

What changed: top_height solves how high straight up over the feet a point must be to show on screen level with the top of the camera-facing, foreshortened picture; Fighter._bar_y puts the health bar and the damage numbers 0.3 m above it.

Why it matters: The bar must not cross the picture's face in any view (Step 22) and must follow the camera (Step 25).

What to check: Finding 1: with Overview's 78 degree pitch a point straight up comes nearer to the camera, which moves it down the screen for a fighter in the lower half; the clamp to 0.1 allows up to ten times the picture's height. At 820x1180 Flarekid's bar shows about 80 px under him (camera-views block). The test only checks that the bar is on the screen.

Concepts: Transform3D.affine_inverseThe inverse of a transform with scale; camera.affine_inverse() * point gives the point in the camera's space, where -z is the depth in front of it. foreshorteningAn upright object seen from above looks shorter by the cosine of the view's pitch; the picture takes 40 % of that (FORESHORTEN), so a point straight up must be solved, not just lifted by the picture's height.

2 · A picture that always faces the camera

hack_star_godot/scenes/toon/cutout.gdshader:35-59 · 20a3da8 · Steps 22-24 · C5, C6, D21, D24

35void vertex() {
36 UV = UV * (1.0 + 2.0 * pad) - vec2(pad);
37 // Mirrored around its middle, the picture's feet would move: the quad moves back under them.
38 if (flip) {
39 VERTEX.x += (2.0 * feet_x - 1.0) * width_m;
40 }
41 VERTEX.xy = mat2(vec2(cos(tilt), sin(tilt)), vec2(-sin(tilt), cos(tilt))) * VERTEX.xy;
42 VERTEX.yz = vec2(VERTEX.y * cos(tip), VERTEX.z + VERTEX.y * sin(tip));
43 // Turned fully to the camera (as BaseMaterial3D's BILLBOARD_ENABLED), keeping the model's
44 // scale. A camera that looks down sees an upright fighter shorter (by the cosine of its pitch,
45 // the camera's up vector's y), so the picture shrinks around its feet by part of that: it keeps
46 // its proportions and stays about as tall on screen as the fighters built from shapes, whose
47 // heads and tops still show from above.
48 VERTEX *= mix(1.0, clamp(INV_VIEW_MATRIX[1].y, 0.0, 1.0), foreshorten);
49 MODELVIEW_MATRIX = VIEW_MATRIX * mat4(
50 INV_VIEW_MATRIX[0], INV_VIEW_MATRIX[1], INV_VIEW_MATRIX[2], MODEL_MATRIX[3]);
51 MODELVIEW_MATRIX = MODELVIEW_MATRIX * mat4(
52 vec4(length(MODEL_MATRIX[0].xyz), 0.0, 0.0, 0.0),
53 vec4(0.0, length(MODEL_MATRIX[1].xyz), 0.0, 0.0),
54 vec4(0.0, 0.0, length(MODEL_MATRIX[2].xyz), 0.0),
55 vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0));
56 MODELVIEW_NORMAL_MATRIX = mat3(MODELVIEW_MATRIX);
57}
58
59// The picture's alpha at `uv`, 0 outside the picture (no branch: the samples stay uniform).

What changed: The vertex shader pads the UV for the outline, mirrors around the middle and moves the quad back under the feet (flip), applies the idle sway (tilt) and the knock-out (tip), then builds a full billboard from the inverse view matrix keeping the model's scale, and shrinks the picture by part of the foreshortening.

Why it matters: One material does every per-fighter effect, so FighterModel's rig, body and recoil code moves the picture like the shape fighters.

What to check: That the model's yaw no longer matters (the quad faces the camera), that flip keeps the feet in place for Echo (feet_x 0.56), and that the picture stays upright whatever the rig's yaw (MODELVIEW_NORMAL_MATRIX follows the new matrix; unused by an unshaded shader).

Concepts: MODELVIEW_MATRIXWritable in a Godot 4 spatial vertex() function; replacing its rotation with the camera's (INV_VIEW_MATRIX columns) turns the quad to the camera, as BaseMaterial3D's billboard mode does. INV_VIEW_MATRIXThe camera's transform in the world; its second column is the camera's up vector, whose y is the cosine of the pitch used for the foreshortening. mat2 rotationmat2(cos, sin, -sin, cos) turns 2D points; here the picture's vertices around its feet for the sway and the lean, since a node rotation would not show on a camera-facing quad.

65void fragment() {
66 vec2 uv = UV;
67 if (flip) {
68 uv.x = 1.0 - uv.x;
69 }
70 vec2 inside = step(vec2(0.0), uv) * step(uv, vec2(1.0));
71 vec4 color = texture(picture, clamp(uv, vec2(0.0), vec2(1.0)));
72 color.a *= inside.x * inside.y;
73 // One screen pixel in picture UV, per axis.
74 vec2 pixel_uv = vec2(length(vec2(dFdx(uv.x), dFdy(uv.x))), length(vec2(dFdx(uv.y), dFdy(uv.y))));
75 float pixels = width_px * max(1.0, min(VIEWPORT_SIZE.x, VIEWPORT_SIZE.y) / 720.0);
76 vec2 radius = pixel_uv * pixels + grow_uv;
77 float ring = 0.0;
78 for (int i = 0; i < RING_SAMPLES; i++) {
79 float angle = float(i) * TAU / float(RING_SAMPLES);
80 vec2 direction = vec2(cos(angle), sin(angle));
81 ring = max(ring, alpha_at(uv + direction * radius));
82 ring = max(ring, alpha_at(uv + direction * radius * 0.5));
83 }
84 float outline = smoothstep(0.35, 0.65, ring);
85 vec3 rgb = color.rgb;
86 float grey = dot(rgb, vec3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));
87 rgb = clamp(mix(vec3(grey), rgb, saturation), 0.0, 1.0);
88 rgb = mix(rgb, vec3(1.0), flash);
89 ALBEDO = mix(outline_color.rgb, rgb, color.a);
90 ALPHA = max(color.a, outline) * fade;
91 if (ALPHA < 0.01) {
92 discard;
93 }

What changed: Each pixel samples the picture's alpha on two rings of 12 points at the outline's screen-pixel radius (plus the grow), so a transparent pixel next to the figure becomes the dark outline; saturation, flash and fade are applied on top, and nearly transparent pixels are discarded.

Why it matters: C6: the outline is as wide on screen as the shape fighters' (ToonMaterials.OUTLINE_PIXELS, scaled with the screen above 720 px); C7: fade gives the see-through in cover without a material swap.

What to check: 24 texture reads per pixel of the quad (cheap at fighter size; Step 28 measured no extra cost); the ring radius per axis from dFdx/dFdy keeps the width in pixels when the quad is foreshortened.

Concepts: dFdx / dFdyScreen-space derivatives: how much a value changes to the next pixel; the length of (dFdx(uv.x), dFdy(uv.x)) is one screen pixel in UV, so a radius in pixels becomes a radius in UV. discardDrops the fragment entirely (no colour, no depth); used for the empty corners of the quad so they never hide what is behind. blend_mixNormal alpha blending; the picture is drawn in the transparent pass, which is why the muzzle star needs render_priority 1 and no depth test to show over it.

70## The halo behind the fighter (null without a pedestal).
71func get_halo() -> MeshInstance3D:
124func _process(delta: float) -> void:
125 if _reveal_time < 0.0:
126 return
127 _reveal_time += minf(delta, MAX_REVEAL_STEP)
128 _apply_reveal(_reveal_time)
129 if _reveal_time >= maxf(REVEAL_SECONDS, HALO_FLARE_SECONDS + HALO_SETTLE_SECONDS):
130 _reveal_time = -1.0

133# The reveal at `time` seconds: the pop (if any), and the halo that flares, then settles.
134func _apply_reveal(time: float) -> void:
135 if _reveal_pop and model.get_rig() != null:
136 var grow: float = Tween.interpolate_value(
137 REVEAL_START_SCALE,
138 1.0 - REVEAL_START_SCALE,
139 minf(time, REVEAL_SECONDS),
140 REVEAL_SECONDS,
141 Tween.TRANS_BACK,
142 Tween.EASE_OUT
143 )
144 model.get_rig().scale = Vector3.ONE * grow
145 var halo_scale: float
146 var halo_alpha: float

What changed: show_fighter skips a repeat of the same fighter and skin, otherwise rebuilds and plays reveal(); the reveal runs on its own clock (at most 1/30 s per frame) and computes the pop, the halo flare and the settle with Tween.interpolate_value.

Why it matters: Home refreshes on every progress change and must not replay the pop; a slow first frame of the fighter screen would otherwise skip the whole 0.45 s pop.

What to check: The early return also applies to stages without a pedestal (harmless: same model); the rig is scaled, not the model, so home's entrance tween on the model is untouched.

Concepts: Tween.interpolate_valueA static helper that evaluates an easing curve at a time without creating a Tween; here the pop (TRANS_BACK overshoot) and the halo are computed from the reveal's own clock. TRANS_BACKAn easing that goes past the end value and comes back; EASE_OUT gives the short overshoot of the pop (about 7 % here). CPUParticles3DParticles simulated on the CPU; used instead of GPUParticles3D because the Compatibility renderer on WebGL limits GPU particles (D23).

hack_star_godot/scenes/arena.gd:365-401 · 65b7ff3 · Step 25 · V1, V4, V5, D25

365## Places the camera for the view in use, part of the way there during a switch.
366func _place_camera() -> void:
276 var pitch: float = deg_to_rad(CAMERA_PITCH_DEGREES)
277 var backwards: Vector3 = Vector3(0.0, sin(pitch), cos(pitch))
278 _camera.look_at_from_position(_camera_target + backwards * _camera_distance, _camera_target)
367 var pose: Transform3D = view_pose(_view)
368 if _blend_left > 0.0:
369 var share: float = smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, 1.0 - _blend_left / VIEW_BLEND_SECONDS)
370 pose = _blend_from.interpolate_with(pose, share)
371 _camera.global_transform = pose
372
373
374## Where the camera stands and looks in the view `view_id` (D25); it always looks north.
375func view_pose(view_id: String) -> Transform3D:
376 var view_data: Dictionary = CameraViews.get_view(view_id)
377 var pitch: float = view_data["pitch_degrees"]
378 match view_id:
379 CameraViews.CLOSE:
380 var target: Vector3 = _follow_point + Vector3(0.0, 0.0, -CAMERA_LOOK_AHEAD)
381 # Like Classic, it does not look so far south that the near wall fills the screen.
382 target.z = minf(target.z, _close_max_z)
383 return _orbit_pose(target, pitch, _close_distance())
384 CameraViews.BEHIND:
385 # `distance` behind the fighter, as high as the pitch towards the look-ahead point.
386 var ahead: float = view_data["look_ahead"]
387 var behind: float = view_data["distance"]
388 var height: float = (ahead + behind) * tan(deg_to_rad(pitch))
389 var eye: Vector3 = _follow_point + Vector3(0.0, height, behind)
390 var ahead_point: Vector3 = _follow_point + Vector3(0.0, 0.0, -ahead)
391 return Transform3D(Basis.looking_at(ahead_point - eye, Vector3.UP), eye)
392 CameraViews.OVERVIEW:
393 var center: Vector2 = ArenaLayout.bounds().get_center()
394 return _orbit_pose(Vector3(center.x, 0.0, center.y), pitch, _overview_distance)
395 return _orbit_pose(_camera_target, CAMERA_PITCH_DEGREES, _camera_distance)
396
397
398# The camera `distance` metres from `target`, south of it, looking `pitch_degrees` down at it.
399static func _orbit_pose(target: Vector3, pitch_degrees: float, distance: float) -> Transform3D:
400 var pitch: float = deg_to_rad(pitch_degrees)
401 var eye: Vector3 = target + Vector3(0.0, sin(pitch), cos(pitch)) * distance

What changed: _place_camera blends from the old pose with a smoothstep; view_pose builds Close (0.6 x Classic's distance, its own near-wall limit), Behind (6 m behind at the height of a 28 degree line to 4 m ahead) and Overview (fitted to the arena's bounds), all looking north.

Why it matters: A fixed yaw keeps the keys' screen direction (V4) and the pictures facing the camera; Classic is unchanged (G11).

What to check: Overview is fitted with Canyon.WALL_HEIGHT for both worlds (Glimmer Isles uses the canyon's heights by design) and does not leave room for the start hint (finding 5).

Concepts: Transform3D.interpolate_withBlends position linearly and rotation spherically between two transforms; with a smoothstep share the camera eases in and out of a view switch. Basis.looking_atA rotation whose -Z points along the given direction with the given up; the camera looks from the eye to the target.

59 _sun.rotation = _sun_rotation
60 else:

64 -deg_to_rad(preset["sun_pitch_degrees"]), _sun_rotation.y, _sun_rotation.z
65 )

67 environment.ambient_light_color = _tint(preset["ambient_color"], _base.ambient_light_color)
68 environment.ambient_light_energy = preset["ambient_energy"]
69 environment.background_mode = Environment.BG_SKY
70 environment.sky = _preset_sky(preset)
71 var balance: Vector3 = Vector3(
72 preset["brightness"], preset["contrast"], LightPresets.saturation(_preset, boost)
73 )
74 environment.adjustment_enabled = not balance.is_equal_approx(Vector3.ONE)

What changed: apply duplicates the world's own environment, sets the sun, ambient and a new procedural sky tinted with 30 % of the world's colours (Classic restores the world's own), the colour balance with K's x1.3 saturation, and glow (Neon night only), then assigns the copy.

Why it matters: The scene's shared Environment resource is never changed, so the next arena starts from the world's own light; one place applies every preset in both worlds.

What to check: adjustment_enabled is off when it would change nothing (Classic without the boost); glow settings are set on every preset but only enabled where the preset says.

Concepts: Resource.duplicateA copy of a resource (shallow by default: sub-resources are shared); the sky is replaced by a new Sky, so the shared one is never modified. adjustment_saturationEnvironment's colour-correction pass (brightness, contrast, saturation) after rendering; supported by the Compatibility renderer, so it works in the web export. glow_hdr_thresholdOnly pixels brighter than this bloom; 0.5 lets the emissive path stones, crystals and shots glow in Neon night.

153# The crystals' glow and the islands' turn and bob at the current time.
154func _animate() -> void:

156 for instances: MultiMeshInstance3D in _crystals:
157 var strength: float = float(instances.get_meta("glow_strength")) * pulse
158 (instances.material_override as ShaderMaterial).set_shader_parameter(
159 "emission_energy", strength
160 )
161 for instances: MultiMeshInstance3D in _islands:

163 (instances.get_meta("transforms") as Array).size(), _island_centers.size()
164 )
165 for index: int in count:
166 instances.multimesh.set_instance_transform(index, island_place(instances, index))
167 for fall_index: int in _waterfalls.size():
168 var island: int = _waterfall_islands[fall_index]
169 var fall: MeshInstance3D = _waterfalls[fall_index]
170 fall.position.y = (
171 _island_centers[island].y

178## Where the part instances of the island `index` is now: turned around the island's axis and
179## lifted by its bob.
180func island_place(instances: MultiMeshInstance3D, index: int) -> Transform3D:
181 var way: float = 1.0 if index % 2 == 0 else -1.0
182 var turn: Basis = Basis(Vector3.UP, way * ISLAND_TURN_SPEED * _time + index)
183 var lift: Vector3 = Vector3(0.0, _bob(index), 0.0)
184 var center: Vector3 = _island_centers[index]
185 var place: Transform3D = instances.get_meta("transforms")[index]
186 return Transform3D(turn * place.basis, center + lift + turn * (place.origin - center))
187

What changed: Every frame the crystal parts' emission_energy pulses by +-60 %, each floating island's MultiMesh instances turn around the island's axis and bob, and the waterfalls follow the bob.

Why it matters: L2 asks for moving decoration without colliders and without re-baking (D12): only the baked transforms and a uniform change.

What to check: Finding 2: the crystal parts' material_override is the shared ToonMaterials cache entry (keyed by colour and glow strength), so the pulse changes the cached material for every user of that key and leaves its last value after the arena closes.

Concepts: MultiMesh.set_instance_transformMoves one instance of a MultiMesh; the islands' parts are moved per instance each frame instead of being separate nodes. shader parameter on a shared materialset_shader_parameter changes the material resource, so every mesh that uses the same ShaderMaterial sees the new value.

Findings

Code review (CODE REVIEW:) of bccd2ed..f10d71c, layer by layer (spec, architecture, code, quick scan). Ran: tools/test.ps1 (516 of 516 passed), tools/lint.ps1 (exit 0), tools/check_tools.ps1 (exit 0), tools/export_web.ps1 in clean worktrees of both revisions (exit 0; 40,516,330 → 41,244,423 bytes; the .pck searched for every excluded name: none); the record checked with change_record.schema.json; a headless probe and windowed screenshots on both sides, plus the views at 820×1180. Good: every Step checked its look on real screenshots and wrote what it changed after looking and where it differs from the plan; one shader carries all the per-fighter effects behind the unchanged FighterModel API, so the idle, run and recoil code and the see-through work for the pictures; the camera never turns, which keeps the controls right in every view; presets are data applied in one place to a fresh environment (a test that the shared one is unchanged); the new decoration has no collider and a test says so; the author's untracked art was kept out of git and the export by a filter and measured in his working tree; performance measured twice per row against a baseline, with a fair re-check using fighters of shapes.

Concepts glossary

Transform3D.affine_inverse
The inverse of a transform with scale; camera.affine_inverse() * point gives the point in the camera's space, where -z is the depth in front of it.
foreshortening
An upright object seen from above looks shorter by the cosine of the view's pitch; the picture takes 40 % of that (FORESHORTEN), so a point straight up must be solved, not just lifted by the picture's height.
MODELVIEW_MATRIX
Writable in a Godot 4 spatial vertex() function; replacing its rotation with the camera's (INV_VIEW_MATRIX columns) turns the quad to the camera, as BaseMaterial3D's billboard mode does.
INV_VIEW_MATRIX
The camera's transform in the world; its second column is the camera's up vector, whose y is the cosine of the pitch used for the foreshortening.
mat2 rotation
mat2(cos, sin, -sin, cos) turns 2D points; here the picture's vertices around its feet for the sway and the lean, since a node rotation would not show on a camera-facing quad.
dFdx / dFdy
Screen-space derivatives: how much a value changes to the next pixel; the length of (dFdx(uv.x), dFdy(uv.x)) is one screen pixel in UV, so a radius in pixels becomes a radius in UV.
discard
Drops the fragment entirely (no colour, no depth); used for the empty corners of the quad so they never hide what is behind.
blend_mix
Normal alpha blending; the picture is drawn in the transparent pass, which is why the muzzle star needs render_priority 1 and no depth test to show over it.
Dictionary.get with default
Returns the default for a missing key instead of an error; here an empty look table for the drawn and picture fighters before their own table replaces it.
property setter
facing_left: set(value) runs code on every assignment (GDScript 2.0); here it updates the shader's flip whenever Fighter changes the facing.
get_viewport().get_camera_3d()
The camera currently rendering the node's viewport; null outside the tree, so _bar_y falls back to an identity camera in tests without a scene.
Tween.interpolate_value
A static helper that evaluates an easing curve at a time without creating a Tween; here the pop (TRANS_BACK overshoot) and the halo are computed from the reveal's own clock.
TRANS_BACK
An easing that goes past the end value and comes back; EASE_OUT gives the short overshoot of the pop (about 7 % here).
CPUParticles3D
Particles simulated on the CPU; used instead of GPUParticles3D because the Compatibility renderer on WebGL limits GPU particles (D23).
_unhandled_input
Called for input events no Control consumed; the arena's HUD buttons get their clicks first, keys reach the arena.
InputEvent.is_action_pressed
True when the event is a press of a key bound to the action in the InputMap; echo repeats are ignored by default.
Transform3D.interpolate_with
Blends position linearly and rotation spherically between two transforms; with a smoothstep share the camera eases in and out of a view switch.
Basis.looking_at
A rotation whose -Z points along the given direction with the given up; the camera looks from the eye to the target.
Resource.duplicate
A copy of a resource (shallow by default: sub-resources are shared); the sky is replaced by a new Sky, so the shared one is never modified.
adjustment_saturation
Environment's colour-correction pass (brightness, contrast, saturation) after rendering; supported by the Compatibility renderer, so it works in the web export.
glow_hdr_threshold
Only pixels brighter than this bloom; 0.5 lets the emissive path stones, crystals and shots glow in Neon night.
MultiMesh.set_instance_transform
Moves one instance of a MultiMesh; the islands' parts are moved per instance each frame instead of being separate nodes.
shader parameter on a shared material
set_shader_parameter changes the material resource, so every mesh that uses the same ShaderMaterial sees the new value.
start_unlocked()
The fighters every save has unlocked; SaveData adds them to older saves, so a new unlocked fighter reaches every player.
exclude_filter
Comma-separated globs of resource paths left out of the export pack; tools and tests are kept out the same way.
